sections.category: Anthropic opens Milan + Seoul offices; Project Glasswing update lands 10,000+ critical findings into the same week

bullets.body: Inside 48 hours either side of the Thursday Series H close, Anthropic stood up two new country footprints and shipped a public update on its Claude Mythos-powered vulnerability program. On Tuesday May 26, Anthropic appointed KiYoung Choi (formerly Country Manager of Snowflake Korea, with prior leadership stints at Google Cloud, Adobe, Autodesk, and Microsoft Korea) as Representative Director of Korea, with senior leadership traveling to Seoul in the coming weeks to formally open the office and meet customers, per [Anthropic Korea](https://www.anthropic.com/news/kiyoung-choi-representative-director-anthropic-korea). On Wednesday May 27, the company opened a Milan office — its sixth European footprint after London, Dublin, Paris, Zurich, and Munich — to serve Italian enterprise, research, and developer communities under GDPR-compliant data residency, per [Anthropic Milan](https://www.anthropic.com/news/milan-office-opening). Bridging both is the Project Glasswing first-update that flowed through trade press across the week, with Claude Mythos Preview credited for 10,000+ high- or critical-severity findings across roughly 50 partners (Mozilla closed 271 Firefox vulnerabilities at 10x its prior rate, Cloudflare surfaced 2,000 bugs of which 400 were rated high or critical), 530 high/critical disclosures to maintainers and 75 patches completed, plus a wolfSSL CVE-2026-5194 certificate-forgery flaw (CVSS 9.1) on a TLS library embedded in roughly five billion IoT, automotive, and industrial-control devices, per [Help Net Security](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/05/26/anthropic-project-glasswing-update/) and [The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/claude-mythos-ai-finds-10000-high.html).

sections.category: SpaceX S-1 vs Musk: $37.5B disclosure gap on the Anthropic Colossus compute deal heading into June 8 roadshow

bullets.body: Thursday saw the disclosure language in SpaceX's May 20 S-1 collide publicly with Elon Musk's own X-post characterization of the Anthropic compute arrangement, leaving roughly a $37.5 billion gap between the two on the day SpaceX confirmed its institutional roadshow opens Monday June 8 at a $1.75T-$2T target range and ~$75B raise. The S-1 describes Anthropic as agreeing to pay a $1.25 billion monthly fee through May 2029 — implying a ~$45 billion three-year commitment — while Musk said on X the arrangement is a 180-day lease with 90-day mutual cancellation, putting the maximum obligation at ~$7.5 billion and adding that SpaceX may reclaim the capacity for xAI "if compute gets super tight," per [The Next Web](https://thenextweb.com/news/musk-spacex-colossus-anthropic-180-day-lease) and [OpenTools](https://opentools.ai/news/musk-spacex-anthropic-180-day-lease). The underlying asset is Memphis Colossus 1 — more than 220,000 NVIDIA GPUs across 300+ MW originally built to train Grok — and the original deal context (Anthropic securing the capacity ahead of an IPO targeted as early as October) was reported May 6 by [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/tech/2026/05/06/anthropic-signs-elon-musk-s-spacex-for-colossus-1-compute-ahead-of-june-ipo). SpaceX confirmed the SPCX ticker on Nasdaq, with pricing scheduled June 11 and first trade June 12, per [TechStackIPO](https://www.techstackipo.com/ipo/spacex) — analysts on the roadshow are expected to press how a 6-month-vs-36-month characterization flows through the revenue projection lines in the prospectus.

sections.category: Figure AI BotQ hits 1 humanoid/hour on F.03; 350+ shipped, 55 this week

bullets.body: Figure AI on Wednesday May 27 disclosed that its BotQ manufacturing facility scaled Figure 03 production from one robot per day to one robot per hour over the prior 120 days — a 24x throughput improvement — pushing total shipments past 350 units across more than 10 product variants, with 55 robots planned for the week and over 9,000 actuators produced, per [Robotics and Automation News](https://roboticsandautomationnews.com/2026/05/27/figure-ramps-humanoid-robot-manufacturing-at-unprecedented-speed/101954/) and [Humanoids Daily](https://www.humanoidsdaily.com/news/figure-claims-production-milestone-as-botq-ramps-up-figure-03-manufacturing). The ramp leans on dedicated assembly lines distributed across 150+ workstations, custom manufacturing software, and tightened supplier quality controls that pushed first-pass yields above 80%, per [Interesting Engineering](https://interestingengineering.com/ai-robotics/figure-humanoid-robot-production-scale-up). The disclosure pulls Figure into the same fixed-cohort-on-the-factory-floor frame that Apptronik's Apollo Gen 2 sits in (10-unit Mercedes-Benz Tuscaloosa cohort cleared 120h zero-MTBF preflight earlier in the week) — humanoid pure-play comps now have two named OEM-anchored counts shipping inside a 14-day window, on top of Tesla Optimus Gen 3's summer-2026 Fremont production-start target. Investors heading into Monday's tape will be parsing whether 1-robot-per-hour at 80% yield is a defensible cost-curve milestone or an aspirational marketing target, given the 2027 commercial-fleet-scale window Apptronik's Series A extension was sized against.

sections.category: Bay Area June-July calendar: Snowflake Summit 26 (Jun 1-4), Microsoft Build (Jun 2-3), WWDC (Jun 8-12), Databricks Summit (Jun 15-18), AI Engineer World's Fair (Jun 29-Jul 2)

bullets.body: The Bay Area conference wave packs into a five-week window starting Monday — registration deadlines are clustered on the May-31 / Jun-6 hinge. Snowflake Summit 26 runs Monday-Thursday June 1-4 at Moscone Center, with the opening keynote Monday at 5:00 PM PT pairing Snowflake CEO Sridhar Ramaswamy with Anthropic President Daniela Amodei and 20,000+ attendees expected; online registration closes Sunday May 31 with full-conference passes at $2,295, per [Snowflake Summit 26](https://www.snowflake.com/en/summit/) and [Snowflake press](https://www.snowflake.com/en/news/press-releases/snowflake-makes-ai-real-at-snowflake-summit-26-featuring-anthropics-daniela-amodei-and-other-industry-leaders/). Microsoft Build 2026 runs Tuesday-Wednesday June 2-3 at Fort Mason Center San Francisco with the Windows Agent Framework slated for open-source MIT-licensed release on day one, Copilot Agent Mode, and a Windows Agent Store marketplace — free online stream, in-person passes via the [session catalog](https://www.thurrott.com/microsoft/334704/microsofts-build-2026-session-catalog-is-now-live). Apple WWDC26 runs Monday-Friday June 8-12 with the keynote Monday June 8 at 10:00 AM PT and an Apple Park in-person event on day one open to registered developers via random lottery, per [Apple Developer WWDC26](https://developer.apple.com/wwdc26/). AI Tinkerers SF hosts its VIP Dinner: Harnessing Agents on Tuesday June 2 with a hand-selected guest list focused on production agentic deployments, per [AI Tinkerers SF](https://sf.aitinkerers.org/p/ai-tinkerers-vip-dinner-harnessing-agents). Databricks Data + AI Summit runs Monday-Thursday June 15-18 across Moscone North, West, and South with 800+ sessions and named speakers from Databricks, Microsoft, OpenAI, NVIDIA, Anthropic, and LangChain per [Databricks](https://www.databricks.com/dataaisummit). AI Engineer World's Fair caps June into early July at Moscone West, Monday-Thursday June 29-July 2, with 250+ speakers across 20+ tracks (Agentic Commerce, Inference, Security, Generative Media, Harness Engineering), 50+ workshops, a stated 6,000+ AI-engineer attendance, and hotel group rates expiring June 6 per [AI Engineer World's Fair](https://www.ai.engineer/worldsfair/2026). Looking further out: GitHub Universe returns to San Francisco Fort Mason on October 28-29, with registration open and standard pricing kicking in early September per the [GitHub Universe FAQ](https://githubuniverse.com/faq); AWS re:Invent runs November 30-December 4 in Las Vegas with registration opening June 16 and early-bird savings through August 25 per [AWS re:Invent](https://aws.amazon.com/events/reinvent/). Anthropic's Code with Claude developer conference keeps livestream replays at [claude.com](https://claude.com/code-with-claude) for those who missed the in-person May 6 SF flagship.
